title: Months after Buc-ee's lawsuit was filed, what stands in the future for Barc-ee's? - NewsBreak
text: MARSHFIELD, Mo. — A Marshfield dog park and pet cafe facing a trademark lawsuit from Texas-based travel center chain Buc-ee’s is responding to the legal situation not only with seriousness, but also with a playful flair that reflects personality and community spirit as they eye new beginnings. In March this year, Barc-ee’s became one of two Ozarks businesses that were hit with federal trademark lawsuits from Buc-ee’s. In the lawsuit filed against Barc-ee’s, Buc-ee’s points to the Barc-ee’s logo as mimicking their logo. “For example, the Barc-ee’s logo copies Buc-ee’s logo’s use of a friendly smiling cartoon animal oriented within a circle with a yellow background encompassed by a black circle,” court documents say. “As other examples, the Barc-ee’s logo also copies the Buc-ee’s logo with the use of a hat placed on a brown animal with a red tongue and black nose.” In a new response to the lawsuit, Barc-ee’s posted this lighthearted satire video on Facebook and Instagram on Monday, June 23, playfully addressing the confusion by emulating fictional “customer reviews” reenacted by Barc-ee’s owner John Lopez in the video. “While we’re handling the legal side seriously, we also decided to respond in a way that reflects our personality and community spirit: with a lighthearted satire video now gaining traction on Facebook and Instagram,” a Barc-ee’s representative said in a release. According to federal court documents, Buc-ee’s and Barc-ee’s have entered into a settlement agreement with certain terms that may take until August 4, 2025, to complete. They’re in the process of completing the terms. Upon completion of those terms, Buc-ee’s and Barc-ee’s expect to file a stipulated dismissal with the court by Aug. 18. However, if the terms are not completed, Buc-ee’s will continue to prosecute the matter after the stay is lifted. What’s next for “Barc-ee’s”? While Barc-ee’s has decided to close its doors at 152 York Dr. in Marshfield, that doesn’t mean it’s the end — rather, it’s just a new beginning. That same building will soon reopen as “Sprouting Spot,” a preschool and daycare serving children ages 2 to 5 years old. “We’re turning the page with something just as meaningful to our community,” a Barc-ee’s representative told Ozarks First. “We couldn’t be more excited about what’s next.” Sprouting Spot isn’t just kindergarten — it’s “life prep,” the rep says. Sprouting Spot’s curriculum is deeply future-focused — combining academic rigor with emotional intelligence, creativity and critical thinking. The curriculum includes daily instruction in language arts and math, along with science, philosophy, art, music, Spanish and American Sign Language Additionally, Sprouting Spot will include project-based learning like inventing playgrounds, designing city maps and growing food in real-time gardens, as well as special enrichment classes in music and golf, led by local professionals. Sprouting Spot will also have indoor and outdoor play zones, a discovery garden and hands-on STEAM experiences. Families in southeast Springfield will be offered a shuttle service to and from the facility. Those who were fans of the Barc-ee’s dog park should known that Barc-ee’s isn’t letting that aspect of the business go, either. The dog park will be relocated to Ozark right next to Fur-st Class Grooming at 4651 N. 20th St. and will be called “Barkside of the Ozarks.” Barkside of the Ozarks is a vibrant indoor and outdoor dog park that will include a splash pad, agility games, enrichment toys and social zones. Additionally, Barkside will also include a coffee bar and small beer and wine menu for pet parents, as well as outdoor entertainment nights and a rotating band lineup coming soon. And naturally, grooming is sticking around, too. Fur-st Class Grooming is expanding to six locations throughout the Springfield and Ozark area. Currently, two locations are under construction at 1929 E Independence St. in Springfield and 4651 N. 20th St. in Ozark. ‘How strong this community really is’ “The support since our closure has been incredible,” the Barc-ee’s representative told Ozarks First. “People are sad to see Barc-ee’s go, and many have shared their frustration about a small, locally-owned business being targeted by a massive corporation.” The Barc-ee’s crew has received heartfelt messages from people saying they no longer support the other brand, and it’s been a powerful reminder of how strong this community really is, the representative said. While the Barc-ee’s team has been focused on preschools, pups and positive vibes, something a little more digital is also on the way.
